p.title: Which kind of source is it?
p.challenge: Think of a copper-plate grant. Press Next and answer each question to find what kind of source it is

nodes.info: Sources are things from the past that give evidence about it.
Coins carry names, symbols and dates of rulers.
Inscriptions are carved or written on hard surfaces such as rock, pillars or copper plates.
Inscriptions on rock, pillars or copper plates are epigraphic sources.

nodes.text: Is it a text or oral record?
nodes.info: Texts like Kautilya's Arthashastra, or oral traditions, songs and family records (genealogies).
Texts such as the Arthashastra; songs and genealogies preserve memory of the past.
Material remains such as tools, pottery, beads, buildings, terracotta figurines and fossils, found by careful excavation.

nodes.text: People grow crops and tame cattle, sheep and goats
nodes.info: At Mehrgarh (Balochistan) people grew wheat and barley and kept animals.

nodes.text: They stay near their fields and build permanent houses and villages
nodes.info: Mehrgarh had mud-brick houses and storage rooms.

nodes.text: Extra food (surplus) is stored, in pots and storage rooms
nodes.info: Pottery was made to store grain.

nodes.text: Some people become potters, weavers and other specialists
nodes.info: Not everyone had to grow food any more.

p.title: River civilisations
p.challenge: Find the 4 river civilisations: Egypt, Mesopotamia, China and the Harappans

points.name: Giza, Egypt
points.info: On the Nile. The Great Pyramid was built as a royal tomb for a pharaoh.

points.name: Babylon, Mesopotamia
points.info: In the land between the Tigris and Euphrates (Iraq). King Hammurabi issued his code of laws.

points.name: Huang He valley, China
points.info: Along the Yellow River. Shang rulers read cracks in oracle bones.

points.name: Mohenjo-daro
points.info: Harappan city on the Indus (Pakistan). Harappans traded with Mesopotamia.

p.title: From kula to mahajanapada
p.challenge: Order how early society grew from a family into a great kingdom

panels.t: Jana: a larger kin group led by a raja, like the Bharatas
Janapada: the land where a jana settled ('set foot')
Mahajanapada: a large, powerful state (texts list sixteen)
Magadha: the most powerful mahajanapada, with capitals Rajagriha and later Pataliputra

p.title: Mauryas to Guptas
p.challenge: Drag the 5 events into time order, oldest on top (BCE years count down!)

events.label: Chandragupta Maurya founds the Mauryan Empire
events.info: Guided by Chanakya, he defeated Dhana Nanda (about 321 BCE). Capital: Pataliputra.

events.label: Ashoka fights the Kalinga war
events.info: About 261 BCE. Moved by its suffering, Ashoka followed Dhamma.

events.label: Rudradaman I's inscription at Junagadh
events.info: About 150 CE. The Shaka ruler records repairing the Sudarshana lake.

events.label: Samudragupta becomes the Gupta king
events.info: About 335 CE. His court poet Harishena praised him in the Prayaga inscription.

events.label: Skandagupta's record: Sudarshana lake repaired again
events.info: About 456 CE, on the same Junagadh rock as Ashoka's edicts.

Village assembly picks committee members by kudavolai

places.name: Raigad

places.name: Nabadwip, Bengal

places.name: Surat
